question: From k measured concentrations of a chemical on the EPA network-formation MEA screen, how closely can the remaining concentrations be forecast across DIV 5/7/9/12 and 17 features?

data.licence: EPA data: US Government work (public domain); bundle and published results: MIT

protocol_origin: NeuroChip Twin v2 R2 protocol: five chemical folds as packaged, five seeded context designs per chemical and k, curve MAE against held-out level means, paired bootstrap over chemicals (4,000 resamples, seed 0, percentile 95% interval).
development: Outer fold 0 only (49 chemicals) was used to choose features and hyperparameters; folds 1-4 (194 chemicals) were not evaluated by any AnchorBoost variant before this freeze.

development_log.config: ridge plus all-output extrapolation features, 5 or 15 designs, alpha 30-1000
boosted residual, base features, early stopping auto, absolute loss
plus cross-DIV features, 600 iterations, lr .05, 63 leaves, min leaf 100
base features plus Hill and analog deviations, 600/.05/63/100
plus six profile principal components, categorical output id, no early stopping
development_log.note: peak memory 4.3 GB from categorical handling; dropped

development_log.config: numeric DIV/feature index instead of categorical id, no components, early stopping on / off

model.name: AnchorBoost
model.training: Each outer fold trains one model on the other four folds, on every C(L,k) design of every training chemical; the analog feature excludes the chemical itself.

primary.metric: curve MAE, mean over the 5 published designs per chemical
primary.comparator: log-linear interpolation (the strongest published baseline at k=3)
primary.statistic: mean paired difference AnchorBoost minus comparator with 95% bootstrap interval

head_to_head.comparator: published neural-process ensemble per-chemical curve MAE (results/trajectory_cv_per_chemical.csv, method neurotrajectory)
head_to_head.claim_rule: "lower error than the published neural process" only if the upper 95% bound is below 0; otherwise report the difference and interval as measured

secondary: all five folds, fold 0 flagged as development
equal-accuracy design: smallest k at which AnchorBoost matches or beats log-linear interpolation at k+1 and k+2 (wells per chemical)
ablations at k=3, folds 1-4: no anchor, no Hill deviation, no analog deviation, no profile components, five published designs instead of all designs
chemicals where AnchorBoost loses most to each comparator
compute: Laptop CPU, one process, about 1.1 GB peak per fold; no GPU, no paid service.
